newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Big Three banks up on privatisation scheme.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Big Three banks up on privatisation scheme.

text.p: Taiwan's "Big Three" state-run banks rose at mid-morning Thursday on price hike hopes linked to the government's privatisation programme for the three banks, brokers said.
With 75 minutes left, Chang Hwa Bank rose T$4.5 or 3.9 percent to T$120, First Commercial Bank gained T$4 or 3.45 percent to T$120, and Hua Nan Bank surged T$5.5 or 4.98 percent to T$116.5.
"Most analysts estimate the future underwriting price of the Big Three would be around T$130 each, so their prices have potential to rise," said Capital Securities manager Alex Chiu.
In mid-April, the Taiwan Provincial Government gave details of a long-planned sale of equity in the Big Three banks, shortening the time for the effort to 14 months from 18 months.
The provincial government's privatisation panel decided to release 15.9 percent of First Commercial's shares, 7.5 percent of Hua Nan's and 4.6 percent in Chang Hwa's, state radio said.
The plan requires final approval from the Provincial Assembly, after which a date for the sale could be announced.
After the share offer, state stakes in the three banks would be reduced to below 50 percent and would be regarded as being privatised. -- Taipei newsroom (5080815)
